business_problem: Nationwide needed to modernize its faster payments platform for 24/7 resilience, scalability, security, and regulator confidence without depending on a single cloud provider.
solution_summary: Nationwide, Accenture, and Form3 re-architected the building society's faster payments platform around MongoDB Enterprise Advanced to run in an active-active, dual-cloud configuration. The team built a self-hosted stretched cluster spanning nine servers in one hyperscale cloud and nine in another, with a five-node MongoDB cluster writing every transaction to both clouds simultaneously. Under normal conditions, payment traffic is split evenly across the two platforms, and if one cloud fails the surviving side continues processing within minutes. Terraform deployments and CI/CD pipelines automate environment creation, letting the bank stand up a full cluster in about four hours while keeping strict control over performance, security, and scaling for this national payments workload.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Enterprise Advanced
solution_components.role: Runs the self-hosted stretched cluster that stores and replicates faster payment transactions across both cloud environments.

data_flow: Faster payment transactions enter an active-active payments platform, are written by a five-node MongoDB cluster to both clouds at the same time, and are processed from either side so service can continue if one provider goes down.
business_outcome: Nationwide delivered a regulator-ready dual-cloud payments backbone with higher availability and resilience, reached production in under eight months, and created a benchmark architecture for nonstop UK transactions.
